name: Zheng-Dao Marrow-Pulse Implant
description: The Zheng-Dao Marrow-Pulse Implant is a biosynthetic communication device installed within the medullary cavity of the radius or ulna, using the conductive properties of bone tissue to transmit low-frequency vibration signals that are interpreted as sound by the wearer's own skeletal structure. The implant draws power from piezoelectric conversion of the wearer's natural muscle movement — walking, flexing, even breathing generates enough current to keep the unit active indefinitely. Incoming transmissions manifest as bone-conducted audio perceived only by the implant's host, with no external speaker or visible hardware to detect.
specifications: {"installation":"Surgical implantation into medullary cavity of radius or ulna; 40-minute procedure under local anesthetic","power_source":"Piezoelectric muscle-movement harvesting; zero external charging required","transmission_range":"200m direct; citywide via mesh relay","frequency":"Proprietary Zheng-Dao bioelectric band (ZDB-7 spectrum)","detectability":"Registers as organic EM noise on standard RF sweeps; requires specialized bioscan to identify","audio_output":"Bone-conducted; perceived only by host","encryption":"ZDB-7 native 2148-bit channel encryption","removal":"Requires surgical extraction; self-destructs if tampered with externally"}
cultural_context: The Marrow-Pulse occupies a deeply uncomfortable space in GLMZ's cultural consciousness. To have one installed is to accept that a corporation has placed hardware inside your skeleton — an intimacy that many find philosophically disturbing even by the setting's augmentation-saturated standards. Among Zheng-Dao loyalists and their contractors, it is a mark of commitment and trust. Among everyone else, it is regarded with a mixture of envy for its capabilities and unease at the implications. The persistent backdoor rumors mean that some handlers refuse to use Marrow-Pulse implants for their most sensitive operations, routing those communications through external hardware instead — which somewhat defeats the purpose.
known_users: Certain black-site interrogators who use them to coordinate during sessions
Wealthy paranoids who want a communication channel that cannot be taken from them
story_hooks: A player character with a Marrow-Pulse begins receiving transmissions on a frequency that doesn't match any known contact — someone has the device's pairing code who shouldn't.
A Zheng-Dao defector claims to have proof of the backdoor channel and wants help extracting data from their own implant without triggering the self-destruct.

A deceased operative's implant is still transmitting six days after their confirmed death — either the body is somewhere it can harvest bioelectric energy, or someone has found a way to keep the unit active artificially.

The party is hired to extract someone from a Zheng-Dao facility; upon meeting the contact, they realize the contact has no idea they've been transmitting their location via a Marrow-Pulse they didn't know they had.
